# World Orogen

> Believable worlds from the ground up: a free studio of planet tools that gets you from a blank page to a world that makes sense. In the browser, no signup required.

World Orogen builds planets the way the scientific worldbuilding guides (Worldbuilding Pasta, Madeline James, Artifexian) teach you to by hand: plates and their history first, then the land, its climate, its water and ice, its rock, and what the land could feed. The science behind each layer is real, simplified and named, so someone who knows the guides can follow what it is doing. Its worlds are possible worlds, not predictions: much of a planet is chance, and what its people make of it is up to the worldbuilder. It runs entirely in the browser using Three.js and requires no installation, account, or payment.

## The tools

- Generate (orogen.studio/generate): a planet in seconds from sliders: its plates and their boundaries today (ridges, rifts, trenches with island arcs, collisions), a past written in closed form (old mountain belts, cratons, hotspot tracks, flood basalts, continents that fit across their oceans), then finished in the background by Evolution's own finish: the full seasonal climate, rivers carved by its runoff, lakes, an ice age, dunes and loess, a satellite view with clouds, rocks, ore and gem deposits, and food. Reshape plates interactively (select several, preview, then rebuild); a planet code reproduces it exactly
- Import (orogen.studio/import): bring an equirectangular greyscale heightmap (Earth, Mars, hand-drawn, or from another tool) onto a 3D globe and run the full climate on it, with its rivers and lakes, its ice age, a satellite view and its food, with optional erosion and sculpting
- Evolution (orogen.studio/evolution): simulates a planet's tectonic history (a supercontinent breaking up, oceans opening and closing, continents colliding and gathering again over up to 1.5 billion years) as a timeline to scrub, with a chosen ending. Any moment can be sculpted in detail: rivers and lakes through the seasons, glaciers and fjords, sand seas, its own climate, a satellite view with clouds from its climate, and detail finer than its mesh when zoomed in. Geology: rock types, and about 35 kinds of ore, fuel, mineral and gem deposits placed by the history, the climate and the rivers, each district with how it formed, plus one map per technological age (Stone, Copper, Bronze, Iron, Industrial) of what a people could reach. Food (beta): what the land could grow by rain or with irrigation, its staple foods, whether its people could farm, herd or gather, and how many it could feed. A whole planet (its history and its detailed moment) saves as one file, to open again later in any browser

## Who it's for

- Worldbuilders who want a scientifically grounded world, and anyone curious to watch a planet form
- Fantasy and sci-fi authors and tabletop game masters (D&D, Pathfinder, etc.) who need a believable map fast
- Artists and game developers who need heightmaps and data for Gaea, Unity, Unreal, Photoshop or other tools

## Key capabilities

- The same views on every tool: terrain with rivers and lakes, satellite with clouds, Köppen climate and every climate layer, geology, food, heightmap, plates — on a 3D globe or a flat map in any of ten projections
- Climate layers in real units for the year, January or July: pressure and wind, ocean currents and upwelling, sea ice, temperature, precipitation, temperature range, rain shadow, aridity, growing season, rain seasonality
- Export maps up to 16,384px wide, every map as colour or as 16-bit data on documented scales (heightmaps, hillshade, temperature, rain, pressure, winds, currents, ice, Köppen classes, rocks, deposits, food), in ten map projections (equirectangular, Mercator, Robinson, Equal Earth, Mollweide, Hammer, Winkel Tripel, orthographic, azimuthal equidistant, Van der Grinten), one PNG or a ZIP with a README
- Shareable planet codes — copy a compact code to reproduce any planet exactly
- Works on desktop and mobile browsers
- No build step, no dependencies to install — pure ES modules

## Using the maps

Maps, heightmaps and images made with World Orogen are the maker's to use however they like, including commercially; the author claims no rights in them. Raw output may not be protected by copyright, and anyone who enters the same planet code or link gets the same planet, so exclusivity isn't possible; what the maker adds on top is theirs. Crediting World Orogen (orogen.studio) is always appreciated. The app's code is free software under the GPL-3.0 (Copyright (C) 2026 Robert Aguilar).

https://orogen.studio/import — Import
https://orogen.studio/evolution — Evolution
https://orogen.studio/v/2.2/ — the previous version, kept online (and orogen.studio/v/2.1/ before it): from 2.1 on, each minor release stays at orogen.studio/v/<major>.<minor>/, so links and planet files open in the version they were made with

## Technical details

- Built with Three.js (WebGL), vanilla JavaScript ES modules
- Fibonacci sphere meshing with Voronoi tessellation
- Braun-Willett stream power erosion, Barnes et al. pit-filling algorithm
- Coupled climate on a fixed 1° grid: seasonal energy balance, derived pressure belts and winds, wind-driven ocean gyres with upwelling (seasonal in the tropics), and a column-water rain budget — a few seconds at any resolution; Köppen from each region's twelve months
- Fully client-side — no server
